Subject: Follow-up from today — cost pressure details and constraints

Thanks again for the demo and the frank conversation today. A quick recap from our side so we have the same frame: 

- Primary pain: token spend for our invoice extraction pipeline — average request length ~3k tokens, heavy duplicates across customers. Current monthly spend on API calls is ~ $42k and trending up.
- Goal: get to a predictable per-month spend we can commit to for 90 days while we validate quality. Procurement is willing to consider a reserved/committed model but will need clear unit economics.
- Constraints: budget ceiling for pilot is $28k/mo (hard cap). If we can’t show a path under that with reasonable accuracy loss, procurement will pause.
- Operational ask: we need a hands-on pilot that demonstrates batching and prefix-caching benefits on our real traces. Also interested in quantization tradeoffs if it materially reduces cost.

Next steps we discussed: you to send a short TCO sketch (batching/cache/quantization levers + expected % cost reduction range) + proposed pilot cadence. Can you include an estimate of token e2e latency change under batching?

Thanks — Evan

Evan — thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers and a proposed plan below. I kept this high level so procurement can scan it quickly; happy to jump on a 20m call to walk through numbers.

1) High-level TCO levers (expected ranges on your workload)
- Batching (dynamic grouping by sequence length / intent): 20–35% token-cost reduction for request patterns like yours (mix of 1–3k tokens, many repeated prefixes).
- Prefix/KV caching (receipt templates + repeated vendor text): 15–30% additional savings when working set fits in cache (we can estimate hit rate once you share traces).
- Lower-precision quantized variant (8->4-bit profile we validated on similar extraction models): 10–25% GPU-cost improvement, varies with accuracy sensitivity.
- Combined stack (batching + cache + quantization) often yields 40–60% lower per-token spend vs direct hosted calls; conservatively plan for ~35% in pilot to account for integration overhead.

Latency impact: with small-to-medium batch sizes we typically see median token latency increase of ~8–20ms (per-token) but end-to-end request latency can be lower for high-throughput periods due to amortization. For interactive, tight-SLO flows we tune batching aggressively to prioritize latency.

2) Proposed pilot (30 days):
- Goal: demonstrate path to <= $28k/mo for pilot traffic and confirm extraction F1 delta <= 2.5% vs baseline.
- Scope: 1 model family forked to a quantized variant, Redwood-managed pilot cluster, prefix cache enabled with a 10k-key warmup.
- Deliverables: weekly cost & accuracy readouts, dashboard access, weekly syncs.
- Ops: we’ll need a 1–2GB sample of anonymized traces (already flagged in your sample_log_extracts) and volume projections (qps, peak/day).

3) Commercial framing
- Option A: committed reserved capacity (fixed monthly) sized to pilot throughput — discounts layered for 3-month commit.
- Option B: metered + soft cap + automated throttling/fallback; tighter SLA not required for pilot but available for Dedicated later.

I attached a short CSV with a first-pass cost model using the numbers you shared (payloom_cost_estimates_2026-07.csv) and a draft SOW (Payloom_SOW_Draft_v1.pdf) to accelerate procurement.

Next asks from Payloom: sample trace bucket (anonymized), confirmation of pilot start window (we can do a fast-start in 7–10 business days), and any procurement contract constraints (po/term length).

If it helps, I can copy our technical PM (Marissa) on the kickoff thread — she’ll handle setup and dashboard access.

Best,
